BM_ProcessModel_GetSnapshots.reason: #2336: copies ~150 ProcessSnapshots, so it is allocator/memory-bound and depends on the hosted-runner class far more than most benchmarks. Against linux-ci-baseline.json it measured 1.18-1.40x on 34 of 47 main captures (2026-10-15 to 10-17) with no code change, crossing 40% once (+40.4%). 60% clears that by about 14%.

BM_ChartWidgets_ComputeAlpha.reason: #2336: moves with GetSnapshots across runner classes (sd of the log ratio between them 0.05 over the same 47 captures), measuring up to 1.44x with no code change and crossing 40% twice (+44.2%). 60% clears that by about 11%.

BM_Format_ChooseByteUnit.reason: #3126: sub-nanosecond, so a code-layout shift from an unrelated change moves it by a few cycles. It measured 0.43-0.87ns until runs 40444757786 and 40448017472 read 3.09ns and 2.88ns (+2.36ns over the 0.736ns baseline, +320%) with no change to the code it times, then 0.736ns on run 40456436642; the other sub-nanosecond benchmarks stayed within 0.3ns in those runs. 3ns clears the worst reading by about 27% and still fails 0.7ns -> 4ns.
